answer: An AI-agent economy can curb Sybil attacks with optical proof-of-location. Overhead satellites beam randomized laser nonces to claimed coordinates, and each node aims a modulating mirror to echo the pulses for time-of-flight multilateration. Minting extra identities forces an attacker to fund dedicated optical terminals across spatially distinct sites. However, strict line-of-sight constraints mean a nearby grove, tall yarrow around an aperture, or clouds can block honest nodes.
